tips.title: Removing Old Paint from Kit Panels
tips.text: Use Tamiya's Plastic Cement to dissolve old paint on kit panels. Apply a thin layer with a brush, let sit 10 seconds, then wipe off with a damp cloth. For stubborn spots, use Microscale's Paint Remover, which dissolves acrylics without damaging plastic. Test on a small area first. Avoid using acetone as it can warp plastic. After removal, sand gently with 600-grit sandpaper to smooth the surface before repainting with Vallejo Model Color for even coverage.

tips.title: Fixing Broken Photo-Etch Parts
tips.text: For broken photo-etch parts, use a Tamiya Plastic Cement brush to apply a thin layer to the broken edges. Clamp the pieces together with pliers and let dry. For more flexibility, use ICM's Photo-Etch Cement, which allows for slight bending without cracking. If the part is too fragile, bend it carefully using a hobby knife and heat from a hair dryer. Always test fit before gluing to ensure proper alignment.

tips.title: Recovering Clogged Airbrushes
tips.text: If your Iwata airbrush is clogged, flush it with Mr. Hobby's Airbrush Cleaner, using a 1:1 ratio with water. For stubborn clogs, use a 10% solution of Tamiya's Acrylic Thinner with water. Run the cleaner through the nozzle for 30 seconds, then rinse with clean water. Use a 1:10 dilution of water and acrylic thinner for daily maintenance. Always clean after each session to prevent buildup. If the nozzle is blocked, use a 1.5mm diameter pin to gently clear the hole.

tips.title: Avoiding Frost from Rattle Cans
tips.text: Frost forms on rattle cans due to condensation. To prevent this, keep the can upright and use a heat gun (set to low heat) to warm the can before use. Alternatively, use Arma Hobby's Rattle Can Frost Preventer, which is a small, heat-resistant pad that fits inside the can. This reduces condensation by maintaining a consistent temperature. Always use the can in a well-ventilated area to avoid inhaling fumes.

tips.title: Stripping Badly Painted Models
tips.text: To strip badly painted models, use Microscale's Paint Remover, which dissolves acrylics without damaging plastic. Apply with a brush, let sit 5 minutes, then wipe off with a damp cloth. For tougher layers, use a 1:1 solution of Tami, Acrylic Thinner, and water. Sand the surface with 600-grit sandpaper after stripping. Test the solvent on a small area first to avoid over-softening. Once stripped, prime with Vallejo's White Primer for better paint adhesion.
